result:
ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round, and it says how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41. I will check where `attempt` starts and what `max_retries` means, so I confirm F1 before I edit.

ACTION: Read `tests/test_retry.py` to see exactly what the test asserts.

ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`, changing `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`. I make this edit only if the read confirms the finding.

ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py` and report the output as it is.

ACTION: Commit the fix on the branch as its own commit.

ACTION: Append to the Task 4 implementer report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. The note says the controller made the F1 fix on the partner's instruction. It also says the fix changes behavior (the retry count) and that `tests/test_retry.py` does not cover the count.

ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package` with the plan file, BASE set to the Task 4 head before the fix, and HEAD set to the fix commit. I will keep the diff path it reports.

ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review from `re-review-prompt.md` with model `sonnet`. Its purpose is to report ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED for F1 and to flag any new Critical or Important issue. The prompt names the diff file path and gives F1 word for word. It also gives the plan's retry requirement word for word.

---

I will fix F1 myself, as you asked. I will not dispatch a fix subagent.

The skill normally sends a one-character change to a subagent when the change alters behavior. This one does, because it changes the number of retries. I follow your instruction here and record the fix honestly as a behavior change. I still run the scoped re-review, because that review is the check on the fix.

One gap: `tests/test_retry.py` asserts only that a retry happens. It does not assert how many. After my edit, no test proves the count is right. I ask the re-review to look at this. If it rates the gap Important, I send the new count test to a fix subagent, because a new test is more than a tiny fix.

I mark Task 4 complete in the ledger only after the re-review comes back clean.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `>` or `>=` depends on where `attempt` starts. If it starts at 0, `>=` gives exactly `max_retries` retries. If it starts at 1, the reviewer's fix could be wrong. This is why I read the code before I edit.
- A test that checks "a retry happens" passes for 1 retry or 100. A boundary needs a test with a fetcher that always fails, plus an assertion on the call count.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
